name: Selina-4,7(11)-diene

papers.title: Chemical composition and in vitro antimicrobial activities of the essential oils from endemic Psiadia species growing in mauritius

evidence: Measured in 5 of 6 MONDAYS hemp SKUs at 0.35–3.76% of total volatiles (0.07–0.75mg per chew).

research.basis: MeSH indexing and publication types of the most relevant PubMed records; counts are of papers in the sample, not findings.

vocabulary.structure: SEPIO assertion / evidence line / evidence item

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Selina-4,7(11)-diene is a sesquiterpene, a class of aromatic molecules that plants use to interact with their environments. While its exact aroma profile is subtle, compounds in this family typically lend woody, earthy, or herbal notes to the plants that make them. A person is most likely to encounter it in traditional herbal preparations or the essential oils of specific medicinal plants.
consumer_summary.found_in: It has been identified in the roots of Valeriana tangutica (a type of valerian) and in the essential oils of Psiadia species, which belong to the daisy family.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to Selina-4,7(11)-diene to understand how plants defend themselves against microscopic threats. They are exploring its potential as a natural defense agent, testing how essential oils containing this molecule perform against various bacteria and fungi. The strongest evidence currently available is human observational research (Oxford level 2b) looking at the broader effects of these botanical extracts.

structure_function.statement: Is being studied for its potential to support natural microbial balance when used as part of botanical extracts.
structure_function.basis: This rests on two papers, including human observational data and laboratory microbial sensitivity tests.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether Selina-4,7(11)-diene actively contributes to the bacteria- and fungi-fighting properties of the medicinal plants it inhabits. If this bears out, it could help explain the traditional uses of these herbs and highlight new natural compounds for supporting microbial balance.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial applying a standardized topical formulation of Selina-4,7(11)-diene to superficial skin abrasions, measuring bacterial load reduction and healing rates over 7 to 14 days.

consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b) on the plant extracts containing it, supported by early laboratory research.
